controls.title: Incident response plan
controls.objective: An incident response plan is documented, assigns roles, includes third parties, and is exercised at least every 12 months.

evidence.description: IR plan and last exercise report

questions.text: Is there an incident response plan with named roles and third-party contacts (insurer, counsel, providers)?
questions.guidance: Partial: plan exists without third-party contacts.

questions.text: Months since the last tabletop or live exercise of the incident response plan

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Incident triage and escalation
controls.objective: Incident reports are triaged, categorized, prioritized, and escalated per defined paths.

questions.text: Do the last 5 incident tickets show triage, category, priority, and escalation recorded?

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Forensic evidence preservation
controls.objective: Incident data and investigation actions are recorded with integrity and provenance preserved.

questions.text: Is there a procedure for collecting incident evidence (logs, images, video) with chain-of-custody records and hashes?
questions.guidance: Partial: procedure without chain of custody.

questions.text: Did the last significant incident include a documented root-cause analysis?
questions.guidance: Ask for the post-incident report. Partial: a post-incident report exists but does not identify a root cause.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Incident notification
controls.objective: Internal and external stakeholders, including regulators, are notified within required times.

questions.text: Is there a notification matrix listing who must be notified (leadership, regulators, customers, law enforcement) and the deadline for each?

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Containment and eradication
controls.objective: Playbooks define containment and eradication steps for the main incident types.

questions.text: Are there containment and eradication playbooks for ransomware, account compromise, and data exfiltration?
questions.guidance: Partial: one or two of the three.

questions.text: Can the response team isolate an endpoint or disable an account within 15 minutes, shown by test or a past ticket?
questions.guidance: Ask for a demonstration or ticket timestamps. Partial: possible, but the test or ticket shows it took longer than 15 minutes.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29
